description_overrides.Tear film: Tear film: a thin surface lipid layer overlies a mixed mucoaqueous component supplied chiefly by lacrimal secretion and including soluble mucins such as goblet-cell MUC5AC. Membrane-associated epithelial mucins form the underlying glycocalyx and support wetting and barrier function. The air-tear interface provides the primary refracting surface; blinking redistributes and renews the film. Tear-film instability contributes to dry-eye disease. This single top sheet represents the whole tear film; it does not resolve its molecular components or simulate breakup.
description_overrides.Conjunctival goblet cells: Conjunctival goblet cells secrete MUC5AC, a gel-forming mucin in the tear film. This secreted mucin is distinct from the membrane-associated mucins of the superficial epithelial glycocalyx. Goblet cells are lost in cicatricial conjunctivitis and vitamin A deficiency. Fifteen enlarged representative cells are restricted to conjunctival epithelium; the conjunctival specimen cut exposes their profiles.
description_overrides.Pre-Descemet (Dua) layer: Pre-Descemet (Dua) layer: the authored representation of collagen immediately anterior to Descemet membrane, described through human donor-cornea dissection studies. Its status as a separate anatomical layer remains debated. In the surgical big-bubble distinction, type-1 cleavage separates deeper stroma from the pre-Descemet tissue and Descemet membrane; type-2 cleavage separates Descemet membrane from the anterior collagen tissue. These are surgical cleavage planes, not normal open spaces. No physiological thickness is inferred from this teaching band.
description_overrides.Endothelium: Endothelium: an intact posterior monolayer of predominantly hexagonal cells on Descemet membrane. Its barrier and energy-dependent transport functions help maintain stromal hydration and transparency in a pump-leak balance. Na+/K+-ATPase supports ionic gradients; bicarbonate-linked transport and buffering participate in fluid regulation rather than acting as a single literal water pump. Adult human cells normally have insufficient proliferative replacement in vivo; surviving cells enlarge and migrate when cells are lost. Endothelial failure permits oedema and loss of transparency. The displayed mosaic is representative, not a cell-density assay.

schematic_limitations: Arrows follow fluid spaces conceptually; they never indicate flow through solid beam material.
The canal mesh is a wall, not a solid lumen fill. Actual overlay routes must be checked inside open lumens on the final output.
Two collector ostia are teaching examples, not an anatomical count or complete drainage map.
No fixed percentage of conventional flow is assigned; production rate, age and alternate routes are outside this specimen.
Pores, giant vacuoles and juxtacanalicular cells are explained at the interface rather than invented as selectable parts.
No ciliary-muscle motion, inlet-valve mechanism, resistance network or pressure simulation is implemented.

inherited_clinical: Epithelial defects stain with fluorescein and heal in days; contact lens wearers are at risk of Pseudomonas and Acanthamoeba keratitis, which can perforate the stroma.
Progressive endothelial cell loss with guttae on Descemet membrane causes stromal oedema, glare and morning blurring; treated with endothelial keratoplasty.
Thinning and conical bulging of the stroma produces irregular astigmatism; collagen cross-linking halts progression.
